PROJECT PLANNING

The First Ground Engineering Meeting: A Decision-Focused Agenda

Use the initial discussion to establish scope, evidence and the next useful action.

In this insight

Begin with the business outcomePut the information on the tableDiscuss interfaces explicitlyFinish with a defined next deliverableFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Begin with the business outcome

The first meeting should explain what the project must enable: basement space, a construction sequence, a tender decision or a revised delivery plan. State the current stage and the decision deadline. A team preparing a feasibility budget needs a different conversation from one ready to appoint a contractor. Setting this context prevents a meeting from drifting into technical detail without resolving the client’s immediate question.

Put the information on the table

Share the current site plan, available investigation information, relevant drawings and known restrictions in advance. Label the status of each document. During the meeting, identify which assumptions materially affect the proposed scope or programme. Keep a visible information-gap list so the group can distinguish a question that can be answered now from one that requires further evidence.

Discuss interfaces explicitly

Walk through retaining works, support, excavation and water management as connected activities. Ask who is responsible for design, approvals, enabling work, operation and handover at each interface. Invite the parties that can make decisions or provide essential information. A meeting that identifies a gap but has no owner for closing it has only moved the uncertainty into the minutes.

Finish with a defined next deliverable

Agree whether the next output is an option note, a site visit, a revised brief, a budget or a formal proposal. Give it an owner, required inputs and a date. Record unresolved issues without pretending they have been settled. The best first meeting creates a short route to a better decision, rather than a long list of general assurances that cannot be checked later.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • State the decision required.
  • Review one current information pack.
  • Leave with an owned next deliverable.
